title: Night over the Atacama
caption: The Milky Way and bright airglow over the Atacama Desert, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: The Milky Way shines brightly overhead in this view from Chile's Atacama Desert. In the background, an orange and yellow shimmer that looks rather like an aurora adds to the quiet beauty of the sky.

The shimmer is airglow, produced by chemical reactions in the atmosphere that give off light. Usually those emissions are not very strong, but they were unusually strong on the night of this photograph, and a display like this is not the norm.

The photograph was taken during the ESO Ultra HD Expedition and is credited to ESO/B. Tafreshi. Unlike an aurora, which is caused by charged particles from space, airglow comes from the atmosphere's own chemistry and is present every night, though usually too faint to notice.

understand.summary: This is a ground-based landscape photograph by B. Tafreshi from the ESO Ultra HD Expedition. The source does not publish camera, exposure or color-processing details.
understand.eye: Even unusually bright airglow is faint, and a camera gathering light over time shows its orange and yellow colors more strongly than the eye.
